scope: A late ELF DSO finalizer reads its original native monitored-fence CPU mapping after the bridge exit hook. The unchanged old interposer crashes with SIGSEGV; three fresh guests using the fix pass. Two further fresh guests retain genuine Mesa GL timeline FD and future GPU queue-ordering results. Every capture has independent shader pixel and native/VM cleanup audits. This is a process-exit lifetime fix, not a full desktop, API conformance, long-run stability or near-native performance claim.
hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 Laptop GPU; Windows driver 32.0.16.1742; WDDM 3.2

separateLegacyCapacityFailure.label: guest-teardown/run-8
separateLegacyCapacityFailure.description: Unchanged legacy V1 OpenGL/FD image reached its 256 aggregate-object limit during the FD test. This is distinct from the finalizer SIGSEGV. It is retained as a failure and not included in successful runs.

earlierIntermittentFailure.label: run-9
earlierIntermittentFailure.description: Legacy probe completed both shader frames and the FD diagnostic, then terminated abnormally during process teardown. Native/VM cleanup passed; this run is not counted as success. Root cause unresolved.
earlierIntermittentFailure.attribution: The original legacy exit-128 run did not report its terminating signal. The deterministic finalizer test establishes a real bug and fix, but does not conclusively identify that historical failure.
